contract.task_clause:
In his discussion of the Divided Line, Plato says that, in contrast to mere belief or opinion, knowledge is a belief for which we give reasons or justifications by appealing:
Option A: to what our senses reveal to us about how things appear to us, not how they  really are.
Option B: beyond the Forms to images of goodness, beauty, and truth obtained from particular objects.
Option C: to what we sincerely believe is true about the Forms based on our experiences in the world.
Option D: beyond sense experience to unchanging ideas (Forms) that are perceived as rationally ordered.
